blocks.text: Dear Joseph:

When we last met, you asked that this letter tell you what our work will cost before it tells you what the work is, since the managers who join you in this buyout will read it with their own savings in mind. That seems to me the right order, so I will begin there: Quillon Harbor Advisors will act as financial advisor to {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} and its management group in the proposed acquisition of the company from its current shareholders, for a fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}, and our work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}.

The fee covers all of the work this letter describes, from our first look at value through to closing, and it does not rise with the amount of debt we help you raise or with the price the group finally pays. We have set it that way on purpose, so that nothing we advise about how much to borrow or how much to offer can be read as serving our interest rather than yours.

Beyond the fee, the company will reimburse our reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, and we will ask you before incurring anything out of the ordinary. We cannot promise the calendar of a buyout in which the shareholders, the lenders and your own colleagues each set part of the pace, though in our experience a transaction of this kind occupies the better part of a year once the first lender has been called.

A management buyout asks the people who run a business to stand on both sides of it for a time, as stewards of the company for its present owners and as the buyers who hope to own it next, and our work is arranged to keep that position manageable. We will act for the management group of Blankenship Inc in this transaction and not for the shareholders, who will need an advisor of their own, and we will say so plainly to anyone who asks.

Our first task is an independent view of what the business is worth to a buyer whose own money is at risk. Angela Cole, an Analyst in our Advisory group, will build that view from management's model and from comparable management buyouts and other transactions of similar size, and we will take you through the range, and the assumptions beneath it, before any figure is put to the shareholders.

The second task is the financing. We will work out how much debt the company can carry without straining it, how much of the price the managers can fund themselves and how much the shareholders might reasonably be asked to defer, and we will then run a confidential process with lenders and other providers of capital covering {{fact:f:E-2018-001.scope}}, a list we will settle with you before anyone is approached.

The third task begins once the shareholders have seen an offer they can take seriously, and it runs to closing. We will help you negotiate price and structure with the shareholders and their advisors, support the lenders through their diligence, and keep the commitment papers, the purchase agreement and the flow of funds moving together, so that no one of them is left waiting on another.

Richard Mccoy, a Partner of the firm, will lead the engagement and will be your first call on any question of value, structure or timing. Thomas Mccoy, an Advisory Associate, will run the work from day to day and will keep the lender materials, the data room and the record of who has received what; Angela Cole will support them both, and I will read every document before it leaves our office.

The work will ask a good deal of you in return. We will need management's model and the monthly results as each month closes, timely access to the company's records and to its senior managers, and the findings of the quality of earnings review the company commissions, because every lender we approach will want to see them.
Fees, Expenses and Invoicing

We will invoice against the fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}} as the work proceeds, together with any expenses incurred in the period, and each invoice is payable on receipt. Should the group decide to pursue a materially different transaction from the one described here, we will propose any change to these terms in writing before we begin the additional work.
Duration and Termination

This engagement takes effect on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}} and continues until the transaction closes or until either of us ends it by written notice to the other. If the group decides not to go forward, a decision we will help you reach honestly if the numbers point that way, the company will owe the part of the fee earned by the work done to that point, together with expenses already incurred.
Confidential Information

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the company and its managers give us, and we will use it only for this engagement. A buyout by management is especially sensitive inside the company itself, so we will deal only with the people you name to us, and until a lender has signed a confidentiality agreement every document we send it will describe the business by its sector and revenue band alone.
Limits on Our Liability

We will bring care and our best professional judgment to this work, but we cannot promise that any lender will commit, that the shareholders will accept an offer, or that a transaction will close on any particular terms. Our aggregate liability arising from this engagement is limited to the fees actually paid to us, neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, and the company will indemnify us against claims by third parties arising from the engagement except to the extent they result from our own gross negligence or willful misconduct.
Governing Law and Entire Agreement

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which Quillon Harbor maintains its principal office, and the courts of that state will hear any dispute that arises under it. It is the whole of our agreement on this engagement and may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.

If this letter reflects what we have discussed, please sign where indicated below and return a copy to me. When it reaches us, Richard Mccoy will send you our first information request and propose a date for the working session at which we will go through management's model together.
Should the Management Group Bid for Blankenship Inc, and Can It Finance the Bid?

To: Richard Mccoy, Angela Cole, James Lawson
From: Thomas Mccoy
Re: Management buyout advisory for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, kickoff
Distribution: engagement team only. Please do not forward this memo or quote from it outside the team.

Our engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}. Joseph Jones, the company's Chief Financial Officer, speaks for the management group and is our day-to-day contact. The group has one decision to make, and this memo sets out the work we will do to inform it.

The decision breaks into four questions. First, what is the company worth to a buyer whose own money is at risk? Second, how much debt can the business carry, and from which lenders? Third, how much equity must the managers put in, and how much of the price must the shareholders agree to defer? Fourth, will the shareholders accept an offer built that way?

The questions are in order of dependence. We cannot size the debt until we know the earnings a lender will accept, and we cannot ask the managers for equity until we know the debt. The shareholders see nothing from us until the first three have answers we can defend.

items: Value. Angela Cole will build a valuation range from management's model, adjusted for owner-related costs, and from comparable management buyouts and other transactions of similar size. She will mark every input as audited, as management's estimate, or as our assumption. Richard Mccoy reviews the range before any figure reaches Joseph Jones.

Debt capacity. Angela will model the debt the business can carry under the terms lenders are offering this year and under the new federal limit on interest deductions. James Lawson will draft the lender teaser and the confidential information memorandum, describing the company by sector and revenue band until each lender has signed a confidentiality agreement. The financing plan will cover {{fact:f:E-2018-001.scope}}; the list will mix senior cash-flow lenders with providers of subordinated capital, and it goes to the client for approval before anyone is called.

Equity and deferred consideration. Richard will meet the managers to learn what each is prepared to invest, and he will test how much of the price could be left in as a seller note or as rolled equity. Individual managers' commitments will not appear in any document that leaves this team.

Shareholder acceptance. Richard and Joseph Jones will decide together when the group's first indication goes to the shareholders, and in what form. Nothing goes to the shareholders or their advisors without Richard's approval.

blocks.text: Several things are outside this engagement. We are not running a sale of the company and will not solicit other buyers; if the shareholders decide to test the market, Richard will raise it with the client and we will revisit the engagement letter. We do not advise the shareholders, we are not giving a fairness opinion, and we give no tax, legal or personal financial advice to individual managers.
The quality of earnings review belongs to the accounting firm the company engages. We will read its findings and carry them into the model, but we do not prepare them and we do not sign them.

Nor do we negotiate the managers' own arrangements with the company after closing, such as employment terms or the split of equity among them. Those belong to the managers and their counsel, and we will decline politely if asked.

I will keep the document log for this mandate. Please send me any draft before it goes to Blankenship Inc, and copy me on anything sent to a lender. Richard is fixing a date for the first working session with Joseph Jones; until then the team will meet each Monday morning.
Blankenship Inc Management Buyout: Briefing for Joseph Jones and the Management Group

items: Quillon Harbor has advised {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} and its management group since {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}} on a proposed purchase of the company from its current shareholders.
The shareholders have agreed to hear a proposal from management. They have not yet seen a price or a structure.
Management's model has been reviewed line by line with Joseph Jones. The company's quality of earnings review is under way.
No lender or other provider of capital has been contacted. Outreach waits on your approval of the list and of the lender memorandum.
The engagement team is unchanged: Richard Mccoy leads, with Thomas Mccoy and Angela Cole.

blocks.text: What the Analysis Shows

items: Value. Angela Cole benchmarked the company against {{fact:f:E-2018-001.comparators}} in the lower middle market. On margins the company compares well. On customer concentration it compares less well, and lenders will ask about it.

Debt. Senior lenders active at this size will lend against the company's cash flow, though probably not enough on their own to fund the price. A second layer of capital, deferred consideration from the shareholders, or both will likely be needed.
Tax. Last December's federal tax legislation caps the interest a company may deduct. The model applies the cap, and it reduces the debt the business can carry comfortably.
Equity. The managers' commitments, as indicated to Richard Mccoy, meet the equity a lender will expect to see. They leave little room if the price moves up.

Seller note. If the shareholders defer part of the price, lenders will require the note to rank behind their debt. We recommend telling the shareholders this ourselves when the indicative proposal goes to them.

blocks.text: Before Outreach Begins

items: Joseph Jones to approve the outreach list, which covers {{fact:f:E-2018-001.scope}}, and to name any lender the group wants left off it.
Thomas Mccoy to circulate the lender memorandum to the management group for comment.
Richard Mccoy and Joseph Jones to agree when an indicative proposal goes to the shareholders, and what it says about financing.
Lender outreach to begin once the quality of earnings draft is in hand.

blocks.text: The main business of the session was lender outreach, the draft quality of earnings report, and the shareholders' response to the indicative proposal for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}. Richard Mccoy chaired. These minutes record the positions reached. They do not record every view expressed.

Thomas Mccoy reported on outreach. The lender memorandum went out after the quality of earnings draft arrived, and meetings between lenders and management have begun. No lender has yet put terms in writing. The questions so far concern customer concentration and the treatment of owner-related costs.

Thomas Mccoy also reported on the data room. Access is set lender by lender, and each lender sees only the folders released to it. The folders on customer contracts and on management compensation remain closed to every lender until written terms are in. Joseph Jones asked that this continue; no one dissented.

Joseph Jones raised the time the lender meetings are taking from the senior managers. Each meeting has run most of a day, including the site tour. Richard Mccoy agreed that later meetings should be shorter, and that a lender which has not read the memorandum before its meeting should be given a later slot.

Angela Cole summarized the quality of earnings draft. In the main it supports management's figures. It accepts the add-backs for owner-related costs that end at closing, and it questions the adequacy of one inventory reserve. Angela has rerun the model on the adjusted figures. The effect on debt capacity is small, but she will not present the revised figures to lenders until the reserve question is settled.

Joseph Jones reported that the shareholders' advisor has acknowledged the indicative proposal. The shareholders want evidence of financing before they discuss price. Richard Mccoy recommended that the group hold its indication where it is until at least one lender has given terms in writing. Joseph raised the strongest objection to that course: the shareholders may read a quiet month as weakness. The group accepted the recommendation. Richard will keep the shareholders' advisor informed of progress without discussing price.

Status Report: Management Buyout Advisory for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}

To Joseph Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Blankenship Inc. From Thomas Mccoy, Advisory Associate, for the engagement team of Richard Mccoy and Angela Cole. This report covers the period since our July working session. It is confidential to the management group and its counsel.
What Happened Since July

The period opened with lender meetings. Management presented the business to each lender that had signed a confidentiality agreement, and Angela Cole sent each of them the customer concentration analysis they had asked for. The later meetings were shorter, as you had asked, because lenders arrived having read the memorandum. The final quality of earnings report then settled the inventory reserve question, on figures close to those in the draft, and Angela updated the model the same week. Written indicative terms began to arrive soon after, and we opened the customer contracts folder to each lender once its terms were in hand. We compared the terms on amount, pricing, amortization, covenants and conditions, and Richard Mccoy took you through that comparison early in August. On that basis the group chose the lenders it will take into confirmatory diligence. Richard then sent the shareholders' advisor a short financing summary, with lender names withheld. The shareholders have agreed to meet on price, and the period closed with that meeting being arranged.
The Figures

Four measures appear in this report, and each stands on its own. The financing plan we agreed in June names {{fact:f:E-2018-001.scope}}; it was set before any outreach began and it has not changed. Outreach is tracked separately, and the tracker shows {{fact:f:E-2018-001.pipeline-lenders-approached}} as of this report. The valuation range still rests on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.comparators}}, the same set we used in June, because the final quality of earnings figures did not move the range enough to call for a new one. The engagement budget is unchanged at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}, as set in the engagement letter, and nothing in this period required work outside it.
The Next Period

The next period should take the selected lenders through confirmatory diligence and toward commitment papers, and take the group into price negotiation with the shareholders. That outlook rests on four assumptions. First, the final quality of earnings figures hold up in lender diligence. Second, trading through the summer stays in line with the model. Third, the shareholders accept that part of the price is deferred, in a seller note subordinated to the senior debt. Fourth, the lenders' credit committees meet on the schedule the lenders have given us.

The third assumption carries the most risk. If the shareholders will not defer any part of the price, the group must either find more equity or offer less. Richard Mccoy will want to discuss both options with you before the price meeting.

For that meeting, Angela Cole is preparing a short paper for the management group that sets the valuation range beside the financing terms now in hand. Richard will take you through it beforehand. The paper will not go to the shareholders' side.
The second assumption is the one we can test soonest. Please send the monthly results as each month closes, so that Angela Cole can update the model before the lenders ask for them.

One risk sits outside the four assumptions. Customer concentration remains the lenders' main concern, and the loss or repricing of a large account before closing would reopen their terms. We know of no such event, and you have agreed to tell us at once if one appears.

The purchase agreement will follow the price meeting. The shareholders' counsel has said it will prepare the first draft, which is usual for a seller. Your counsel and Richard Mccoy will review it together, and Angela Cole will check every defined financial term against the model.

Confirmatory diligence will be heavier than the first round. The lenders will want site visits, a review of the principal customer contracts, and their own counsel's review of the purchase agreement once a draft exists. I will run their requests through a single list, so that management answers each question once.
This report describes lender terms in general only. Please keep it within the management group of Blankenship Inc and its counsel until the price meeting has taken place.
Working Session Notes: Blankenship Inc Management Buyout

Joseph Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Blankenship Inc
Thomas Mccoy, Advisory Associate, Quillon Harbor Advisors

blocks.text: First topic: the financing commitments for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}. Thomas Mccoy confirmed for the record that lender outreach closed with {{fact:f:E-2018-001.pipeline-lenders-approached}} over the summer, and that no further lender will be contacted unless the selected group withdraws. The senior lender's draft commitment letter is in hand. Its covenants are close to the term sheet, but it adds a minimum liquidity test the term sheet did not contain, and its market flex language is wider than the group accepted at term sheet stage. Angela Cole confirmed that the base case meets the liquidity test in every month of the model, with the narrowest margin at the seasonal low in working capital. The subordinated lender's terms are unchanged from its term sheet and were not discussed. Richard Mccoy recommended accepting the liquidity test and pushing back on the flex. The strongest objection is that pushing back costs goodwill with the lender, and the group may need that goodwill on later points. Joseph Jones agreed with the recommendation. Where it landed: the liquidity test is accepted, and a markup narrowing the flex goes back to the lender.

Second topic: the purchase agreement and the seller note. The shareholders' counsel has returned the first draft of the purchase agreement, and the price agreed at the shareholders' meeting stands. The open point is the seller note. The senior lender requires the note to be fully subordinated, with no payments while a default continues and a standstill on enforcement. The shareholders' counsel accepts subordination but resists the length of the standstill. Richard Mccoy proposed a shorter standstill in exchange for a modestly higher interest rate on the note. Angela Cole said the model can carry the higher rate without pressing on the senior covenants, subject to her rerun. Joseph Jones asked that the proposal go to the management group before it goes to the shareholders, and Richard agreed. The working capital target in the draft follows the quality of earnings figures and was not discussed further. Where it landed: subordination is agreed in principle, and the length of the standstill remains open.

Richard Mccoy will send the flex markup to the senior lender. Once the management group has agreed, he will put the standstill proposal to the shareholders' counsel. Thomas Mccoy will reconcile the commitment letter against the term sheet line by line, keep purchase agreement drafts within the working group, and update the closing checklist. Angela Cole will rerun the model with the higher note rate and the liquidity test and send the result to Joseph Jones. Joseph Jones will take the standstill proposal to the management group of Blankenship Inc and confirm the group's position to Richard.

The next session will be set when the shareholders' counsel responds on the standstill. Thomas Mccoy will circulate the reconciled commitment letter beforehand, so that the session can take it as read.
